title: Tentative-output handoff: model arbitration, acceptance scoring, and fallthrough playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a runtime mechanism that allows a fast, tentative output path to produce early tokens with an automated handoff to the primary decoder when acceptance confidence is low. This ticket captures the arbitration policy, acceptance scoring signals, and a deterministic fallthrough playbook for graceful degradation. The goal is to reduce median latency for interactive workloads while bounding misprediction cost and ensuring deterministic behavior for streaming clients.
rationale: Customers require low tail latency for chat/assistant features, but we must avoid regressions in output quality and cost. A lightweight tentative path (smaller or kernel-optimized model, or an aggressive attention truncation) can produce early tokens faster; we need a standard way to score and accept those tokens and to fallback to a full-quality decode when necessary. This reduces wasted work and keeps SLOs predictable.
proposed_solution: 1) Define an acceptance score computed at each tentative token boundary composed of: log-prob delta vs primary model (estimated via lightweight estimator), entropy threshold, n-gram overlap to recent context, and KV-cache freshness heuristic. 2) Implement an arbitration layer in the runtime that: (a) schedules tentative path work under a strict time budget, (b) collects acceptance signals, (c) decides accept/continue/rollback deterministically. 3) Add a fallthrough circuit that, upon rejection or timeout, either (i) streams replacement tokens from the primary decoder, or (ii) issues a soft-rollback token event for clients that can patch streamed content. 4) Expose early-accept-rate, rollback-rate, and token-cost-delta in Console and use them for canary gating.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance score defined and documented with signal weights and units
Runtime arbitration shim implemented in serving runtime with a 1-2ms median decision overhead
Deterministic fallback behavior for streaming clients (no duplicated tokens or out-of-order commits)
Canary traffic experiment plan with shadow mode and staged rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100%)
Telemetry surfaced in Console: early_accept_rate, early_reject_rate, rollback_rate, extra_tokens_generated, p50/p95 latency delta
No regression in a held-out quality eval set beyond 0.5% user-visible metric degradation
tasks: Spec: formalize acceptance score formula and edge cases
Runtime: implement tentative worker pool and arbitration API
Kernel integration: ensure selected kernels for tentative path are compatible with KV cache sharing
Streaming contract: define token patch protocol and client-side expectations
Telemetry: add metrics and traces for each decision boundary
E2E test: synthetic scenarios for low-confidence and high-confidence handoffs
Canary rollout: define gating thresholds and automation runbook
